bullets.title: CLS: Monster Beat/Raise — FY27 $40B Revenue, $21.50 EPS Guide Well Above Street
bullets.body: Celestica reported Q3 EPS $3.30 vs consensus $2.96 on revenue $5.83B vs $5.46B. FY27 guidance of $40.0B revenue and $21.50 EPS crushed consensus of $35.87B/$19.84, implying ~90% Y/Y revenue growth; EBIAT margins guided to 9.0% vs 8.7% consensus. Stock reversed a 6% intraday drop to close +13-17%. Top 3 customers (GOOGL 35%, META 17%, AWS 14%) drive concentration risk but validate AI infrastructure thesis.

bullets.title: GLW: Optical +44% Y/Y Drives Beat/Raise; Citi PT $220 (72% Upside)
bullets.body: Corning Q3 core EPS $0.91 beat guidance of $0.85-0.89 and Street $0.88 on revenue $5.08B vs $5.03B consensus; optical segment $2.38B was +44% Y/Y and 7% ahead of Bloomberg consensus, with enterprise optical up 84%. Q4 guidance of $0.96-1.00 EPS and $5.2-5.3B revenue topped Street $0.93/$5.20B. FCF $661M massively beat Street $274M. JPM maintains Neutral awaiting Springboard targets; Citi Buy with $220 PT at 32x CY28 EPS.

bullets.title: AVGO: DA Davidson Upgrades to Buy ($400 PT); Backstops $63B Anthropic Chip Financing
bullets.body: DA Davidson (Gil Luria) upgraded Broadcom to Buy from Neutral, raising PT to $400 from $350, citing the $63B debt financing package arranged for Anthropic's TPU chip procurement — the largest AI infrastructure debt deal ever. Broadcom CEO Tan negotiated higher rates and provided guarantees; deal structured via SPV to reduce upfront funding concerns. Stock +2.5% premarket. Multiple sources flag AVGO as primary AI ASIC design house with residual value support on the deal.

bullets.title: CDNS: Beat/Raise for Third Time This Year; JPM Raises PT to $420
bullets.body: Cadence raised FY26 revenue guidance to $6.387-6.417B (midpoint $6.402B vs prior $6.30B) and EPS to $8.37-8.43 ($8.40 midpoint vs $8.10 prior), with op margin 44.2-45.2%. Record backlog of $8.2B; 18% YoY organic recurring revenue growth. Agentic AI tools expected to drive higher EDA tool consumption with a new consumption-plus-subscription model. JPM OW, PT raised to $420; Citi raised FY26/FY27 EPS estimates 2%/4%.

bullets.title: META: $97.5B Equity Offering with NVDA $3B Investment; EPS Headwind from $95B+ AI Capex
bullets.body: Meta priced ~$97.5B equity offering at $625/share (common + convertible preferred); NVDA investing $3B as part of expanded AI collaboration, with AMD and AVGO also participating. OpCo notes the $95B capex program lowers 2027/28 EPS estimates 14-15% below Street and increases 2027 share count ~4%, with valuation range $676-$845. META down 0.3% premarket on dilution; Hedgeye maintains bearish trend signal.

bullets.title: DASH/CART: Acquisition Talks Advanced at ~$17B; Wolfe Models 11x 28E EBITDA Post-Deal
bullets.body: DoorDash is in advanced/exclusive talks to acquire Instacart for ~$17B, with an announcement potentially imminent. Deal is primarily equity with ~80mm shares of dilution; analysts model ~$100M revenue synergies and ~$100M EBITDA synergies, implying DASH trades at ~11x 28E EBITDA post-close. Regulatory scrutiny cited as key hurdle; investor feedback mixed (bearish near-term, constructive medium-term). Wolfe Research hosting a 2pm call on strategic rationale. CART winding down Caper Cart operations by end of Q2 2027.

bullets.title: HUBS: UBS Downgrades to Neutral — Mixed SMB Demand, AI Monetization Friction
bullets.body: UBS (Taylor McGinniss) cut HubSpot to Neutral from Buy citing uneven SMB/new-logo growth and nascent AI monetization; FY27 constant-currency revenue growth falls to 13% from 14.5%. Stock +30% in the past month at ~12x CY27 EV/FCF leaves balanced risk/reward. HUBS -2.9% premarket.

bullets.title: RCL: Strong 3Q Beat; 2027 EPS 'Will Have $20 Handle'; Mizuho PT $380
bullets.body: Royal Caribbean reported Q3 adj. EPS $6.57 vs guidance $6.26-6.36 and Street $6.36; EBITDA $2.54B beat Street $2.47B (+11% Y/Y). Full-year EPS guidance raised to $17.85-17.95. 2027 booking volumes +high-teens at higher prices; customer deposits +8%; management guided to a '2027 $20 handle' on EPS. Citi maintains Buy with $362 PT (14x FY27 EBITDA); Mizuho raises PT to $380. Stock +6% premarket.

bullets.title: HLT: RevPAR Guide +100bps to 4.0-4.5%; EPS Raised 15c; EBITDA Leverage Muted by Middle East Fees
bullets.body: Hilton raised FY26 RevPAR guidance to +4.0-4.5% (vs prior +3.0-3.5%, Street +2.6%) and Q4 RevPAR to +3.0-3.5% (vs prior implied +0.5-2.5%). Q3 RevPAR +5.8% beat guide of +4%; EPS $2.45 beat guide $2.28-2.34. FY26 EPS raised +1-2% to $9.07-9.13 but EBITDA only narrowed to higher end of $4.06-4.08B (vs historical 1:1 flow-through) due to Middle East incentive fees and timeshare timing slipping to 2027. UBS maintains Buy.

bullets.title: AAPL: Hedgeye Flash Call — Remains Short at 38x FY27 P/E; China Share Loss Flagged
bullets.body: Hedgeye is hosting a flash call reiterating short AAPL at record highs. Key concerns: 38x FY27 P/E unjustified by single-digit growth, China losing share in non-premium smartphone segment, iPhone Duo showing mixed signals/display issues, and memory headwinds persisting into 2027. GS notes AAPL guided F4Q26 iPhone revenue +15% Y/Y with gross margins 47.8% (including 1pp tariff benefit), but Hedgeye sees November 2nd guidance disappointment risk.

bullets.title: VZ: Strong Wireless Adds (406K vs 186K Est.) But MS Cuts PT to $50; Citi Buy at $53
bullets.body: Verizon posted 406K postpaid phone net adds in Q3 vs consensus 186K; broadband nets +314K (fiber +155K, FWA +159K). FY26 guidance raised: EPS $5.04-5.06, FCF approaching +12% Y/Y. AI Connect scaled to ~$4B signed contracts. Morgan Stanley cut PT from $52 to $50 (EW) on higher-rate environment and Starlink/AI deflationary risks. Citi maintains Buy, cuts PT to $53, and highlights 10-15mm broadband TAM expansion potential from AI fiber/fixed wireless.

bullets.title: SHOP/FIG: Citi Sees Q3 Beats Ahead; SHOP Q4 Growth Approaching 30%
bullets.body: Citi models SHOP Q3 revenue growth ~300bps above Street at 34.5% Y/Y, driven by Merchant Solutions +38%; raises Q4 GMV and revenue estimates 100bps+ above consensus targeting growth approaching 30%. TP moved to $216 (55.4x FY28 EV/FCF). FIG modeled at 43% Q3 growth with ~$19M revenue beat on seat expansion and AI Full Seat upgrades; TP moved to $35 (7x FY28 EV/S). Both report next week.

bullets.title: BKNG: Opco Top Pick on AI-Driven Multiple Compression; ABNB PT Raised to $210-215
bullets.body: BKNG has de-rated ~30-34% YTD, near parity with EXPE on 2027 P/E; Opco views this as the best entry since Oct 2022 and names it top pick as AI disruption fears have compressed the multiple. ABNB PT raised to $210-215 (from $190) by both OpCo and OPCO on lower AI exposure, hotel expansion, and accelerating nights growth — ABNB has outperformed BKNG by +55% YTD. EXPE viewed as most exposed to AI disruption and seen as crowded short.

bullets.title: SPHR: MS Maintains OW, Cuts PT to $150 on Softer Wizard of Oz; Rocky Horror as 2027 Catalyst
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley cut SPHR price target from $170 to $150 (maintains OW, >30% upside) due to softer-than-expected late-summer Wizard of Oz attendance. Q3 Experiences revenue lowered to ~$110M; Q4 expected to see ~25% sequential increase on Vegas rebound. Rocky Horror Picture Show launching early 2027 seen as meaningful catalyst; new Sphere location announcements remain a potential catalyst over the next 6-12 months.

bullets.title: TKO/FWONK: GS Previews Q3 with Below-Consensus EBITDA; Middle East Cancellation Risk
bullets.body: Goldman (Buy, $215 PT) expects TKO Q3 Adj. EBITDA of $537M vs consensus $556M, with UFC strength offset by weaker WWE; flags up to ~$50M (~2%) FY26 EBITDA risk from potential Middle East event cancellations. FWONK (Buy, $116 PT) expected to post F1 revenue $1.125B vs consensus $1.104B with Adj. OIBDA $324M vs $322M, supported by stronger sponsorship and an extra race YoY. Both report this week.

bullets.title: VST/TLN/GEV: Power Price Dynamics Diverge; GEV Turbine Pricing +60% YTD
bullets.body: VST should modestly beat Q3 EBITDA but lower power forwards cut PT to $164 (Buy, ~11% FY29E FCF yield). TLN faces PJM concentration risk with lower forwards reducing PT to $371 to Hold, though $50+ FY28 FCF/share on buybacks possible. GEV turbine pricing surged ~60% YTD to $2,200-2,300/kW with new units approaching $2,900-3,000/kW, reinforcing the power-supply bull case.

bullets.title: DKNG: NY Sports Betting GGR Down 16% YoY in September; Handle Share Erosion
bullets.body: New York total online sports betting GGR fell 17.7% YoY to $159.4M in September 2026. DraftKings GGR declined 16.0% YoY to $56.0M; handle share fell to 35.0% from 38.1% YoY. CZR dropped 27.4% YoY. Overall market conditions soft with hold compression across operators.

bullets.title: EQIX: Morgan Stanley Top Pick on 49GW Power Shortfall; $1,250 PT
bullets.body: MS named Equinix its top pick in communications infrastructure, citing a 49GW utility power shortfall expected by 2028E (327GW demand vs 278GW supply) and 11% Y/Y contract pricing increases. Global data center IT capacity forecast to reach 316GW by 2030E at 23% CAGR. YE27 PT of $1,250.

bullets.title: Upcoming Earnings This Week: GOOGL, MSFT, AMZN, NOW, STX, INTC, PINS Key Catalysts
bullets.body: Major universe names reporting this week: GOOGL and MSFT on Wed (10/28, consensus EPS $3.02/$4.71); NOW on Wed (consensus $1.02); STX on Tue after close (consensus $7.45); AMZN and INTC on Thu (consensus $1.97/$0.41); PINS on Thu (consensus $0.49). JPM flags hyperscaler capex commentary and AI demand signals as the key read-throughs for the broader semis/infrastructure trade.

bullets.title: AI Positioning: Semis Net Exposure at 17th Percentile After Hedge Fund De-Risking; Squeeze Risk Elevated
bullets.body: Multiple desks flag that hedge funds de-risked concentrated AI/semis positions, rotating into hyperscalers; semiconductor net positioning at 17th percentile creating a potential short squeeze if hyperscaler earnings deliver capex confirmation. Semis ETFs saw record ~$12.7B inflows on the dip (SOXX +$6.5B, SOXL +$2.8B, SMH +$2.6B). CTA equity exposure at 11th percentile; a 2% S&P decline estimated to trigger ~$155B of forced selling.
